transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm just really struggling with how my face looks, especially my skin and the shape of my nose. I feel like my skin is covered in awful scars and my nose is completely crooked, even though everyone else tells me it looks totally fine. It's making me incredibly unhappy and I just can't focus on anything else.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time checking your reflection in mirrors or performing other repetitive actions, like picking at your skin, to try to fix or hide these perceived flaws?

Yes, I spend hours compulsively checking any mirror I can find, and I often pick at my skin trying to smooth out the scars. It is incredibly exhausting and distressing because I just can't seem to stop myself.

Are your thoughts and behaviors focused specifically on concerns about your physical appearance, or do you also feel driven to perform these repetitive actions to prevent some other unrelated harm or disaster from happening?

No, it's not about preventing any kind of disaster or harm. Everything I do is purely because I am so obsessed with how ugly my skin and nose look, and I'm just desperately trying to fix or hide them.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Body Dysmorphic Disorder, Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder]. The patient clarified that the repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, skin picking) are exclusively driven by concerns about physical appearance rather than the ritualistic behaviors intended to prevent unrelated harm characteristic of OCD. Therefore, Body Dysmorphic Disorder is the primary diagnosis.
